root_cause_hypothesis:
Scored outcome is a clean PASS (build 1 / bp_clean 1 / golden_match 1) on the FIRST build - no compile-fix cycles. The grounding topic under test, get_knowledge(topic="query-object-model"), was ACCURATE and SUFFICIENT: every claim it makes was independently confirmed this run - RANGE-before-join vs QueryFilter-on-the-joined-result; query.addQueryFilter(qbds, fieldStr(T,F)) returning a QueryFilter; SysQuery::value / ::valueNot / ::range / ::valueEmptyString / ::findOrCreateRange / ::findOrCreateQueryFilter all existing with the documented shapes (::range carries a third optional treatOnlyNullAsUnbound); addLink + relations(false) + joinMode(); and [ExtensionOf(classStr(SysQueryRangeUtil))] public static class X_Extension with [QueryRangeFunction()] public static str compiling in a real object, not just a probe. Nothing in the topic had to be worked around.

TOOL_DEFECT 1 (blocks the case instruction literally): d365fo_file(action="create", objectType="class") applies the class-EXTENSION naming heuristic to any objectName ending in "_Extension" and infixes the model prefix before the suffix, with no opt-out. Passing the already-correct, already-prefixed ConDemoRanges_Extension produced ConDemoRangesCon_Extension - prefix at BOTH ends - and rewrote the declaration to match. The heuristic assumes every _Extension class is a CoC wrapper named after its base class, which is false for the SysQueryRangeUtil range-function pattern: an [ExtensionOf] class that only ADDS new static members is conventionally named after what it contributes (Microsoft's own shipped one is SysQueryRangeUtil_Extension in Foundation, and the case asks for <Prefix>Ranges_Extension). No grounded path produces that name; the golden had to pin the tool output. Fix shape: only infix when the passed name actually starts with the base object name, and make prefixing idempotent (a name already starting with the prefix is already final).

TOOL_DEFECT 2 (dead-end guidance): prepare(mode="create", objectType="class", objectName="DemoRanges_Extension") classifies the object as class-extension and fails naming validation with "baseObjectName is required for extension types (class-extension)" - but the prepare schema has NO baseObjectName parameter. The error asks for something the caller cannot supply. It still returns a usable groundingToken, so it is guidance noise rather than a hard block, but it is unactionable as written.

VALIDATOR_GAP 1 (self-reference): validate_code(mode="references") flags a class calling its OWN static methods as unknown-type (5 errors here, e.g. ConDemoQueryRanges::countCustomers). The declared class/table name in the submitted source should seed the local symbol table before the index is consulted; this shape hits every new class with a static helper, which is very common. The printed advice - search("ConDemoQueryRanges") - can never succeed for an object that does not exist yet.

VALIDATOR_GAP 2 (kernel enum, known family): JoinMode::OuterJoin -> unknown-static-member ERROR. Same root cause as the documented kernel-enum allowlist gap (NoYes, TableGroup, ...) but reached through the static-MEMBER rule rather than the type rule, so the warning-not-error downgrade does not apply and the message misdescribes a kernel enum as a class ("Static method OuterJoin not found on JoinMode", "Use get_object_info(objectType=class, name=JoinMode)"). JoinMode should join the kernel-name allowlist and the downgrade should be inherited by the static-member and intrinsic-target rules - this is the second consecutive run in this session reporting the same inheritance gap (see the L2-lookup-reference-multiselect record).

TOOL_DEFECT 3 (silent omission): get_object_info(objectType="class", name="SysQuery", options={"members":"names"}) listed 80 members but SysQuery::range was NOT among them, while non-members were: a bare macro line "#ISOCountryRegionCodes" and two doc-comment sentences ("Deletes ranges in Q which is in InitQ.", "Method to test a packed queryrun container is legal.") appear as if they were members. A targeted options={"method":"range"} read returned the real public static str range(anytype, anytype, boolean=false). The extractor appears to take the line preceding the method body when a macro or stray comment sits between the doc block and the signature, consuming the signature it should have emitted. A member list that silently DROPS a public API is worse than a slow full read - it argues the API does not exist.

TOOL_DEFECT 4 (minor): table fieldFilter is a plain substring match, so "AccountNum|CustGroup|Blocked" on CustTable reported "0 of 193 matching". The name invites a pattern; either support alternation or document substring semantics in the option description.
